findings.title: Scrub mode, the default, misses the most common ways credentials are passed on a command line
findings.evidence: uv run python docs/review/probes/verify-7/privacy_recheck.py (out: privacy_recheck.out.txt): 'LEAK curl bearer header -> curl -H Authorization: Bearer FAKEtok...', 'LEAK mysql attached -p -> mysql -uroot -pFAKEpw-7x db', 'LEAK curl -u user:pass', 'LEAK bash -c wrapper -> bash -c tool --api-key FAKEtok...', 'LEAK docker --env=NAME=value', 'LEAK conn string ...Password=FAKEpw-7x;'; controls hidden ('mysql --password [redacted]', '-e API_TOKEN=[redacted]', 'https://alice:[redacted]@'). Re-ran d-privacy/redact_leaks.py: output identical, '84 cases, 71 of them not controls; 70 leaked in all'. Cause: redact.py:74-79 hides by name only for '-flag value' or NAME=value with the name before the first '='; everything else goes to redact_text (redact.py:47-52: 5 token shapes + scheme://user:pw@). argv[0] is never scrubbed (redact.py:67). Promise: docs/04-features.md:43 'Command lines are scrubbed of secrets before they are stored'; docs/14:192 'Errs towards hiding too much.' Attribution uses the live argv (rules.py:84-86), so the stored form does not affect attribution numbers.
findings.impact: Bearer headers, attached -p passwords, user:pass, wrapped shells and connection strings reach raw/*.db (48 h) and the process drill-down API. The R04 fix does not hold for these forms, and docs/04:43 and docs/14:192 state the opposite.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md:146, docs/08-configuration.md:104, docs/04-features.md:43: make exe_only the default; describe scrub as opt-in and best-effort ('hides known shapes; it cannot recognise every credential'). docs/14:192: drop 'Errs towards hiding too much' or qualify it. src/submeter/core/config.py:186 and raw.py:64,247: default 'exe_only'. Add the redact_leaks cases as a test that records which forms scrub misses.
findings.cost: Three sentences, a default in three places, one test
findings.decision_question: Default redaction: keep scrub (best-effort, misses common forms) or switch to exe_only (no arguments stored; loses detail in the process drill-down, not attribution numbers)? Recommendation: exe_only by default, scrub opt-in and documented as best-effort.
findings.verification: Re-ran redact_leaks.py (identical counts) and wrote my own probe with six common forms plus controls; all six leaked, controls hidden, so the probe is wired correctly. Read redact.py:62-83 and tests/test_baseline.py:171-194 (tests only the handled forms). Searched docs for a stated limit on scrub: none; docs/14:192 claims the reverse. Changed the framing: '70 of 71' comes from a corpus built around the redactor's blind spots, so it is not a prevalence figure; the title now says what is verified. Severity kept at high because the fix for a critical prior finding (R04) fails under real conditions; no fixed rule is broken since nothing leaves the machine.

findings.title: exe_only keeps argv[0], which is a whole process title when a process rewrote it
findings.evidence: redact.py:64-65 'if mode == "exe_only": return (args[0],)'. privacy_recheck.out.txt P2: 'readable non-empty command lines: 290 / NUL split gives one string with spaces (a direct /proc reader): 64 / psutil argv[0] contains a space, so exe_only stores it whole: 12 / exe_only on a one-item argv: ('postgres: alice appdb 10.0.0.5(5432) idle',)'. psutil splits titles without a trailing NUL on spaces (.venv psutil/_pslinux.py:1763-1771), so through the baseline provider (psutil_provider.py:69) only NUL-padded titles stay whole. docs/17:71 'On Linux, read /proc directly' means the planned provider would see all 64 unless it copies psutil's split. scrub mode also keeps argv[0] unscrubbed (redact.py:67).
findings.impact: The strict mode, documented as 'stores the executable only' (docs/17:146, docs/08:104), stores whole titles (user, database, client address for postgres) for 12 processes here via psutil and 64 via a NUL-only reader. No secret was shown in such titles, so this breaks the promise rather than leaking credentials.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/privacy/redact.py (or raw.py:153-154): in exe_only store sample.exe, the executable name, never args[0]. In scrub mode, split an argv[0] that contains spaces and scrub it like the rest. Test with ('postgres: alice appdb 10.0.0.5(5432) idle',). docs/17 Collection: the /proc provider splits a one-string cmdline as psutil does.
findings.cost: About 5 lines plus one test and one sentence
findings.verification: Wrote my own count probe comparing a NUL-only split with psutil.cmdline() on live processes (counts only). The lead's 64 holds for a NUL-only reader but the baseline provider (psutil) stores the whole title in only 12 cases, because psutil splits on spaces when the data has no trailing NUL; corrected the claim that psutil passes titles through unsplit. Downgraded high to medium: the evidence shows identifying titles, not secrets, and no job or gate fails. Added that scrub mode never scrubs argv[0] (redact.py:67). Windows not checked (psutil splits there in C).

findings.title: One process with a non-UTF-8 argument or name stops every raw write while it lives
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P3 (a child started with argument b'caf\xe9-FAKE'): 'psutil returns the last argument as 'caf\udce9-FAKE'' / 'scrub bad item is last arg: ticks ['UnicodeEncodeError' x3]; system_raw rows 0' / 'exe_only bad item is last arg: ticks ['ok' x3]; system_raw rows 3' / 'exe_only, bad character in exe: UnicodeEncodeError'. Mechanism: whole tick in one transaction (raw.py:96); command text bound at raw.py:154-155 and sample.exe at raw.py:164; sqlite3 cannot encode a lone surrogate, so system_raw, workload_raw and process rows roll back; the key never enters self._memory (raw.py:132-133), so every later tick retries and fails. No gap row is written. psutil decodes with the filesystem error handler (surrogateescape; psutil/_common.py:141-142).
findings.impact: Any local process with a Latin-1 argument (scrub mode) or a non-UTF-8 executable name (both modes) blinds the collector with no gap recorded, so attribution, live diagnosis and trends lose the period silently. On Linux other users' processes are read too.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/raw.py _register (or once in the provider): pass every text field (command text, exe, workload, event detail) through text.encode('utf-8', 'backslashreplace').decode('utf-8'). Test with a b'caf\xe9' argument and a non-UTF-8 exe. docs/17 Operations: 'A record that cannot be stored is replaced by a marker; it never fails the tick.'
findings.cost: About 5 lines, a test, one sentence
findings.verification: Ran my own probe with a real child process (not a hand-made string) to confirm psutil produces the surrogate, then wrote three ticks per mode: scrub fails every tick with zero system rows; exe_only survives a bad argument but not a bad exe name, which widens the lead's claim to both modes. Searched R01-R37: none covers encoding. Windows behaviour with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates not checked. Note: docs/review/probes/verify-7/p3_surrogate.py, an earlier file in this folder that I did not create, fails ruff (SIM105); I left it unchanged because existing files may not be edited.

findings.title: redact_patterns has no validator and no way into the store
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P4: 'Settings accepts the pattern '(': ('(',)' / 'redact_cmdline with '(' raises PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0' / 'RawFile parameters: ['path', 'cpu_points', 'memory_step', 'redaction']' / 'RawStore parameters: [..., 'redaction']'. config.py:185-187 has no validator, while Rule.cmdline is validated (rules.py:69-73). grep: redact_patterns is used nowhere else in src. redact.py:66 compiles extra patterns on every call, and they run per argument (redact.py:81).
findings.impact: `submeter config check` accepts an invalid pattern that, once wired into the write path, would raise inside the tick's transaction and fail every tick (as in P3). docs/08:105 'Add your own secret formats' does nothing in the baseline.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core/config.py Privacy: a field_validator that compiles each pattern and names the bad one. src/submeter/store/raw.py: RawFile and RawStore take redact_patterns, compile them once in __init__, pass them at line 154. Add a test.
findings.verification: Re-ran the checks in my own probe: confirmed. Downgraded medium to low: 'never applied' is unbuilt wiring (docs/17:241 build order item 6, privacy.redact), not a defect in a running path. What remains verified is the missing validator, which is inconsistent with Rule.cmdline validation, and an interface that cannot take the setting.

findings.title: Logs, validation errors, reprs and event rows bypass the store's redaction
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P5: 'repr(ProcessCounters) contains the secret: True' / 'str(ValidationError) contains the secret: True' (cmdline given as one string) / 'redact_text on a log line keeps the secret: True' ('launch failed: tool --api-key FAKEtok...'). models.py:19 sets only extra and frozen; cmdline and cwd at models.py:77-78 and 111-112 have no repr=False. raw.py:190-193 record_event stores detail as given. Promise: docs/17:137 and docs/06-storage.md:19 'with the same redaction as the store'.
findings.impact: A log line built from a record, an exception or a provider error can carry the unredacted command line into logs/*.log (25 MB kept) or event rows, in either redaction mode.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core/models.py:19 add hide_input_in_errors=True; Field(repr=False) on cmdline and cwd at models.py:77-78 and 111-112. docs/17:137 and docs/06:19: 'Logs never contain command lines, working folders or the token: they name a process by pid and executable, and validation errors are logged without input values.' Event details are structured fields, never free text taken from a process.
findings.verification: Reproduced (a), (b) and (c) with my own probe; read raw.py:190-193 for (d). Corrected the lead's line numbers (models.py:17 -> 19, 75-76 -> 77-78, 109-110 -> 111-112). Did not re-fetch the Pydantic config page (medium finding); behaviour reproduced locally instead. Searched docs for a rule keeping command lines out of logs: none.

findings.title: Scrub hides harmless arguments, and cmdline rules match text the user never sees
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P6: 'python [redacted]' (script path, no extension), 'optimizer --passes [redacted] model.onnx', 'trainer --tokenizer [redacted]', 'git -C [redacted] status', 'claude --resume [redacted]' (UUID); control 'tool --max-tokens 4096' kept. Causes: _OPAQUE (redact.py:36) includes '/' and '-' so long POSIX paths and UUIDs qualify; _SECRET_NAME (redact.py:21-25) is an unanchored search, so 'pass' hits --passes and 'token(?!s)' hits --tokenizer. Rules match the live argv (rules.py:84-86), so a rule copied from the stored text can miss.
findings.impact: The process drill-down loses the arguments that tell agent sessions, checkouts and scripts apart (live diagnosis). A cmdline rule written from the shown text may never match, leaving CPU Unattributed.
findings.proposed_change: If scrub stays (see P1), src/submeter/privacy/redact.py: anchor _SECRET_NAME to whole words of the flag (bounded by start, '-', '_' or end); exempt strings with a path separator or UUID shape from _OPAQUE; add tests. docs/17 Interfaces: cmdline rules match the unredacted live command line, and `submeter rules test` reads the live process and marks which arguments the store hides.
findings.cost: About 6 lines plus tests, one sentence
findings.verification: Reproduced five of the lead's cases with my own probe. docs/14:192 accepts over-hiding of commit hashes only. Severity stays medium; it falls to low if P1 makes exe_only the default, because scrub then becomes opt-in.

findings.title: Data folders and files are created 0755/0644, readable by other local users
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P7 (umask 0022, temporary SUBMETER_HOME): 'dir 0o755 home/data', 'home/data/raw', 'home/state'; 'file 0o644 .../2026-11-20.db', '-shm', '-wal'; 'file 0o644 home/state/collector.pid'; only 'collector.lock' is 0o600 (files.py:222). Code: files.py:119 mkdir(parents=True), raw.py:66-68 sqlite3.connect default mode, files.py:230 write_text. Rule: docs/17:146 'Restrict every data file and the API token to the current user.' Fix works on POSIX (d-privacy/private_files.out.txt: dirs 0700, db/-wal/-shm 0600). Python docs (re-fetched https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/os.html#os.mkdir): 'On Windows, a mode of 0o700 is specifically handled to apply access control to the new directory such that only the current user and administrators have access. Other values of mode are ignored.' and 'Changed in version 3.12.4: Windows now handles a mode of 0o700.' pyproject.toml:5 requires-python '>=3.12'.
findings.impact: On a shared Linux machine, or with SUBMETER_HOME outside a private folder, other users can read process names, workloads and stored command lines. A token file written the same way would expose the whole API.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/files.py ensure(): create each level under the Submeter root with os.mkdir(path, 0o700) and chmod existing levels on POSIX. src/submeter/store/raw.py: os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_RDWR, 0o600) before sqlite3.connect. Pid file and token: os.open(..., 0o600). Backups into a file made 0600 first. pyproject.toml: requires-python '>=3.12.4'. doctor flags any Submeter path readable by others. Tests under umask 0022.
findings.cost: About 25 lines in files.py and raw.py, tests, one line in pyproject
findings.verification: Re-ran the modes with my own probe under umask 0022 and re-fetched the Python os.mkdir docs. Mitigation: Ubuntu's default home folder is 0750 and %LOCALAPPDATA% sits under the per-user profile, so the default paths are partly protected; SUBMETER_HOME (files.py:48-51) can point anywhere. The two leads state the same problem; kept D-privacy#7's wider evidence and fix.

findings.title: The brief does not say how each client carries the token, and the obvious browser designs put it in URLs, logs or cookies
findings.evidence: docs/17:148 'Require a token on every HTTP and WebSocket request ... and check Origin on the WebSocket'; grep finds no transport, cookie or CSP rule in docs/. docs/05:37-39: dashboard, CLI and agents all reach the API with the token. MDN (re-fetched https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket): syntax is only 'new WebSocket(url)' and 'new WebSocket(url, protocols)'. RFC 6265 (re-fetched) section 8.5: 'Cookies do not provide isolation by port.' Origin scope disagrees: docs/17:148 (WebSocket only) vs docs/17:272 and docs/15:25 ('requests ... with a foreign Origin are refused'). redact_leaks.out.txt: a '?range=1h&token=' URL survives scrub.
findings.impact: A browser cannot send an Authorization header on page load or on a WebSocket, so a builder falls back to a query-string token (access logs, history, the browser's command line) or a cookie sent to every localhost port. The phase-4 gate passes for each of these designs.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md 'Privacy and local security': CLI and MCP send the token in an Authorization header read from the token file. The dashboard shell is served without a token and never embeds one; the CLI opens it with the token in the URL fragment, which the page moves to sessionStorage and strips. API calls use the header; the WebSocket sends the token as its first message and is closed without it within 2 s. No cookies; a query-string token is refused. Host and Origin are checked on every HTTP, WebSocket and MCP request. Access logs omit query strings. rotate-token closes open WebSockets. Phase-4 gate: logs and raw files from the test run do not contain the token.
findings.cost: One paragraph and one gate clause
findings.verification: Re-read docs/17:148, 272, docs/15:25 and docs/05:37-39; grepped docs for a token transport (none). Re-fetched MDN and RFC 6265 and found both quoted sentences. Did not re-fetch the uvicorn source for the access-log format (medium finding). R04's fix names the token and the Host and Origin checks only, so it does not cover transport.

findings.title: Clients send the token to whatever holds the port, and the default 8787 is Wrangler's dev-server port
findings.evidence: Re-ran d-privacy/port_first.py (loopback only): 'the stand-in, which is not Submeter, received: ['Authorization: Bearer FAKE-api-token']' / 'a server starting afterwards cannot bind the port: Address already in use'. config.py:197 and docs/08:107 default port 8787. Cloudflare (re-fetched https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/): 'port: Port for the local dev server to listen on. Defaults to 8787.' docs/05:37-39: CLI and agents use the API with the token. No document covers port-in-use handling.
findings.impact: With `wrangler dev` running, Submeter's server cannot start and the CLI and MCP send the token to the Worker and show its answers. On a multi-user machine another user can hold the port while the server is down and collect the token.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17 'Privacy and local security': after binding, the server writes state/api.json (port, pid, start time, 0600); clients read the port from it, connect to literal 127.0.0.1, and confirm the listener before sending the token (pid check, or an HMAC(token, nonce) challenge); if the port is taken, the server refuses to start and names the holder. docs/08:107 and config.py:197: a default not used by common dev servers, or 0 written to api.json.
findings.cost: Three sentences and one default value
findings.verification: Re-ran the port probe and re-fetched the Wrangler docs. A same-user squatter gains nothing because it can read the token file, and Windows 11 work machines are usually single-user, so the realistic case is a collision with a developer tool. Severity stays medium (cheap to fix, and a server that cannot start leaves live diagnosis unavailable). Windows SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE and localhost resolution order were not checked.

findings.title: Documents disagree on what MCP withholds, and findings may carry command lines into history and MCP
findings.evidence: docs/17:148 'The MCP server must never return command lines or working directories'; docs/17:193, docs/08-configuration.md:125 and docs/05-data-flow.md:50 name command lines only; gate docs/17:274 'no MCP response contains a command line'. AGENTS.md:41 'A command line is redacted before it is stored, logged, put in a finding ...', so findings may hold (scrubbed) command lines; findings live in history.db, 'Kept' (docs/06:15), and docs/17:152 gives findings 'the evidence that triggered them' with no restriction.
findings.impact: Working folders can reach MCP with no gate testing for them. A command line put in a finding outlives the 48 h raw retention and is served to agents through findings, against the MCP rule; with scrub's misses (P1) that can include credentials.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:148, docs/17:193 and docs/08:125: 'The MCP server returns workload names, numbers, findings and verdicts only: never command lines, working folders, executable paths or the token. This limits what reaches an agent's context; it does not stop an agent running as the same user from reading the data files.' docs/17 Analysis: 'Evidence names workloads, executables and metrics, never a command line.' AGENTS.md:41 (owner approval): drop 'put in a finding'. Gate docs/17:274: 'no MCP response contains a stored command line, a working folder or the token'.
findings.verification: Re-read all five passages and AGENTS.md:41. Changed the emphasis: the 'courtesy, not boundary' point is documentation clarity (low); the verified problem is the inconsistent lists plus AGENTS.md:41 allowing command lines in findings, which are kept forever and readable through MCP. The claim that a hosted agent sends tool results to its model provider is inference and was not used for severity.

findings.title: FastAPI's default /docs and /redoc pages load scripts from a CDN, and the brief does not forbid external references
findings.evidence: FastAPI (re-fetched https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/how-to/custom-docs-ui-assets/): 'By default, those files are served from a CDN.' and 'The first step is to disable the automatic docs, as by default, those use the default CDN.'; download links point to cdn.jsdelivr.net (swagger-ui-dist@5, redoc@2). docs/17:38 names FastAPI; docs/17:39 'Use a canvas chart library such as uPlot' does not require it to be bundled; docs/04:37 'Self-contained HTML reports' is not defined. uv (re-fetched https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/sync/): 'when uv run is used, the project is locked and synced before invoking the requested command.' docs/17:199 does not say what the scheduled task or unit runs.
findings.impact: A default build serves pages that make the user's browser contact jsDelivr when opened, against the not-configurable 'sending nothing off the machine' (docs/17:193, AGENTS.md fixed rule 3). A CDN script would also run in the API's origin. No measured data leaves, and it needs a user to open /docs or a builder to use a CDN asset.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md 'Stack and conventions': 'Create the FastAPI app with docs_url=None, redoc_url=None and openapi_url=None. Every script, style, font and image the dashboard and reports use ships in the package and is served by the server; no page references another host. The dashboard sends Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self'; reports carry a meta CSP default-src 'none' with hashes for inline code. The scheduled task and the systemd unit run the installed entry point, not uv run.' Add a test that fails on any http(s):// reference in the built front end or a report.
findings.verification: Re-fetched the FastAPI and uv pages and found the quoted sentences. Downgraded critical to high: the brief itself breaks no rule, and the break happens only in a default build when /docs is opened or a CDN asset is copied, with no Submeter data sent. Dropped the brief.html Google Fonts point as a product issue: brief.html is the design brief page (docs/README.md:58), not the dashboard, and it matters only if copied, which the no-external-reference rule covers. The uv run point is conditional because the brief names no command for the task (suspected part).

findings.title: The WSL guest collector's 'ingest API' conflicts with the loopback-only, read-only API, and default WSL networking cannot reach host loopback
findings.evidence: docs/16-review-log.md:81 (R05 fix) 'The ingest API accepts a second collector'; docs/17:79 'Design the ingest path so a second collector running inside the guest can report to the host'; docs/17:254 API 'read-only except session markers'; docs/17:50 programs 'share nothing but files on disk'. Microsoft (re-fetched https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking): 'By default, WSL uses a NAT (Network Address Translation) based architecture'; 'If you want to access a networking app running on Windows ... from your Linux distribution (ie Ubuntu), then you need to use the IP address of your host machine.'; 'you may need to bind your application to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1'; mirrored mode needs 'Windows 11 22H2 and higher' and a .wslconfig setting, then 'Connect to Windows servers from within Linux using the localhost address 127.0.0.1'.
findings.impact: Phase 7, which can move to right after phase 2 (docs/17:264), either binds beyond loopback under default WSL (breaks fixed rule 3), depends on the user opting into mirrored mode, or adds a write route and hands the token to a guest VM.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:79 and the R05 fix text in docs/16:81: name a transport with no network path and no ingest route. Preferred: the host collector starts the guest collector through wsl.exe and reads its samples from stdout as one more provider, so the host collector stays the only writer of raw files. Do not specify SQLite raw files written through /mnt/c in WAL mode.
findings.decision_question: Guest collector transport: (a) host collector runs the guest collector via wsl.exe and reads stdout, no network and no new file writer; (b) guest writes closed, non-WAL files under /mnt/c that the host imports after close; (c) loopback API under mirrored networking (Windows 11 22H2+, .wslconfig change, a write route, the token in the guest). Recommendation: (a).
findings.verification: Re-read the cited lines and re-fetched the Microsoft networking page; every quoted sentence is present. Changed the proposed fix: the lead's 'raw files through /mnt/c' would put a SQLite WAL database across the VM boundary, and SQLite says (re-fetched https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html) 'All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.' That sub-point is suspected (not run under WSL). Option (a) rests on Microsoft's filesystems page: 'Run Linux binaries from the Windows Command Prompt (CMD) or PowerShell using wsl <command>' and piping works (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/filesystems).

findings.title: The lock's pid file outlives a crashed holder, so a pid-based daemon stop could signal an unrelated process
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P13 (child takes InstanceLock and exits via os._exit, skipping release): 'holder() returns a pid: True; that pid is alive now: False' / 'lock can be taken again: True'. files.py:229-230 writes only os.getpid(); holder() (files.py:233-238) returns it unchecked; only release() deletes it (files.py:243-244). docs/17:199 `daemon start|stop|status|install|uninstall` does not say how stop finds its target.
findings.impact: Pids are reused. A stop built as 'signal holder()' after a crash can end an unrelated process of the user, breaking observe-only (fixed rule 1).
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/files.py: write 'pid create_time' to the pid file; holder() returns None unless a non-blocking lock probe fails (lock really held) and the live process's create time matches. docs/17 Operations: '`daemon stop` asks the program to exit (an API call, a stop file or the service manager) and never signals a pid it has not verified.'
findings.cost: About 10 lines plus a test, one sentence
findings.verification: Reproduced with my own child process in a temporary folder. The risk is latent: a stop through the service manager (scheduled task, systemd user unit) signals no pid, and docs/14:281 calls the pid a convenience, but holder() is the only handle the baseline offers. Medium kept.

findings.title: Workload names are not validated: reserved names can be claimed, and markup or paths pass through
findings.evidence: privacy_recheck.out.txt P14: Rule accepted workload 'system', 'submeter', '', '', '../../x'; a user rule {workload='system', exe=miner} gives 'aggregate rows: [('system', 1), ('unattributed', 1)]'. rules.py:56 'workload: str' unconstrained; reserved names at rules.py:34-37 (SYSTEM is declared but the attributor never assigns it); aggregate merges by name (rules.py:205). docs/17:98 reconciliation has a 'system' term and docs/17:182 ties overhead_fraction to workload 'submeter'. docs/brief.html:5418, 5423, 5428, 5508 insert w.name with innerHTML.
findings.impact: A natural rule such as workload = "system" for svchost or systemd merges user processes into the System row and the reconciliation's system term. `run --as submeter` would inflate the overhead_fraction alert. Unchecked names reach run file names, group names and, if the mock is copied, dashboard HTML.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core: one WorkloadName type, ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$, refusing reserved names (system, restricted, unattributed, submeter, machine) unless the attributor assigns them; AlertRule workload patterns use the same set plus '*'. Use it for Rule.workload and `submeter run --as`. docs/17 Dashboard: 'Insert text from data with textContent, never innerHTML' (this also covers process and executable names, which any local process chooses). Add a test.
findings.cost: About 10 lines plus a test, one sentence
findings.verification: Reproduced the accepted names and the merge with my own probe; confirmed the four innerHTML lines in brief.html. Checked the proposed pattern against every example name in docs/08 and examples/rules.toml ('agent:*', 'opaque:wsl', 'browser', 'ide', 'agent:untagged', 'builds'): all fit, with '*' needed only for alert patterns. R29 limits how many names exist, not which ones.

findings.title: Recorded fixtures from the work computer would be pushed to a public repository; only command lines must be redacted
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:41 covers command lines only ('... or written into a test fixture'). ProcessCounters carries exe, cmdline and cwd (models.py:76-78). docs/13-build-list.md:46 and docs/17:256 ask for 'recorded fixtures for every provider and detector'. prompts/01-execution-prompt.md:3 'on my Windows 11 work computer'. CLAUDE.md:10 'Push freely ... No push here waits for my approval.' The task brief states the repository is public.
findings.impact: A recorded snapshot of a managed work computer (security products, internal tools, user and host names, folder paths) becomes public on the first push. Fixed rule 3 is a product rule, but this sends the same machine data off the machine through the build.
findings.proposed_change: AGENTS.md after line 41 (needs the owner's approval), or docs/17:256 if not: 'A recorded fixture is anonymised before it is written: user name, host name and home folder replaced; executable names outside an allow-list replaced with stable placeholders; command lines in exe_only form; working folders dropped. A test fails if any fixture contains the current user or host name.'
findings.cost: Two sentences and a test of about 20 lines
findings.decision_question: Where the fixture-anonymising rule lives: AGENTS.md after line 41 (owner approval required; applies to every session) or docs/17 'Also deliver' (no approval needed but weaker)? Recommendation: AGENTS.md, with the same sentence in docs/17.
findings.verification: Re-read AGENTS.md:36-46, CLAUDE.md:10-12, prompts/01:3 and docs/13:46; no rule covers exe names, paths or host and user names in fixtures. Did not query the repository's visibility (it would put the repository name into a web request); took it from the task brief, as the lead did. Medium kept: it affects buildability and the owner's data, not a number or a product rule.
